title: [recoverability] Secrets by name, part A: the mask (every form of a known value as [SECRET:NAME]), spawn mask on a stream and spawn mask-hook as a PostToolUse hook, failing closed; installed nowhere
prompt:
Spawn, mission 4, objective 117 [recoverability]: secrets by name, part A. A mask replaces known secret values with `[SECRET:NAME]` in every form a program prints them. `spawn mask` puts a stream through it. `spawn mask-hook` is a Claude Code PostToolUse hook that replaces a tool's response holding a known value. It is built and tested with made-up values only: nothing installs the hook in any settings.

Read sync/design-secret-injection.md: section 0 (the owner's decisions of 11-13: agents keep root, nothing is injectable), 3.4 (the mask) and 5.A. Also the lead's probe in sync/queue.md, "lead 10:22 — hook probe: a PostToolUse hook's replacement is what the session file keeps".

Why. Every leaked value in the record reached a transcript through output an agent saw. Deny rules (108, 113) refuse the known ways of printing. The mask is the second net: output that holds a known value is masked before it reaches the agent, and so before it reaches a transcript, the gateway or a backup. The broker (part E), the services' log writers (part D) and the transcript archiver use it later. This part is the library and its two entry points, and switches nothing on.

Required behaviour.
The values file:
- `NAME=value` lines; `#` comments and blank lines are ignored.
- A NAME is upper-case letters, digits and `_`. The same NAME on several lines gives its current and retired values, all masked as that NAME.
- Mode 600, named by `--values <file>`. A value is never on an argv.
- A value shorter than 8 bytes is refused: masking a common short string would break every output.
Forms masked, for each value:
- plain and JSON-escaped;
- URL-encoded with upper- and lower-case hex (which is also the password in a `user:password@` URL);
- base64 at each of the three alignments, in the standard and URL-safe alphabets (the characters that do not depend on the neighbouring bytes);
- hex in both cases.
Longer forms win at the same place. Forms shorter than 6 bytes are not used.
`spawn mask --values <file>`:
- stdin to stdout through the mask, as it streams.
- An overlap window as long as the longest form, less one byte, waits for the next read, so a value split across two reads is caught.
`spawn mask-hook --values <file>`:
- It reads the PostToolUse event's JSON on stdin.
- When any form of a value is in `tool_response`, it prints `{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PostToolUse", "updatedToolOutput": <the response with every string masked, every other field as it was>}}`.
- Otherwise it prints nothing. It exits 0.
Both fail closed:
- A values file that cannot be read, has group or world access, holds a line that is not NAME=value, holds a short value, or holds no value at all makes `spawn mask` exit 2, having printed nothing of its input.
- The same makes the hook print a replacement that withholds the whole response (a sentence holding no value), as does an event it cannot parse (not JSON, or cut short) or a stdin it cannot read.
- Errors name the file and the line number, never a value.
Not done here, and later steps with the owner's word: installing the hook in any settings (the engines' --settings in bridge.rs included), anything a running session reads, the value store (part B), and the broker (E).

What it does not catch (section 4 of the design): a value transformed in another way (reversed, split, encrypted), values it is not given, and a value the model itself types (it passes no PostToolUse hook). The lead's probe covered Bash only; Read, Grep and MCP tool results are the same hook event and are masked the same way, but no probe has shown what their session files keep.

Files (expected; no other open objective touches them): crates/spawn-cli/src/mask.rs (new) and crates/spawn-cli/src/main.rs (the two commands' dispatch and usage lines). One crate. Size, an exception decided by the lead (11-13), as for 114: about 500 lines in all (R2, after rev-e's F1/F2: +53), about 315 of code (the hook about 80 of them), 59 of doc comments and 122 of tests. It is one crate and one new file, and a split would put mask.rs and main.rs in both halves.

Unit tests: every form at each alignment; a value cut at every byte between two reads; the hook replacing only a response that holds a value, and withholding on a values error and on an event that is not JSON, cut short, or empty; the URL-safe base64 forms of a fixed value whose base64 holds + or / at each alignment.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/117.sh. Black box, with made-up values under a scratch HOME: a current value of BB_ONE holding `:`, `/` and `+`, a retired value of BB_ONE, a value of BB_TWO, and a value of BB_THREE whose fixed start (bb-made-up???value-) gives its base64 a + or / at every alignment, so its URL-safe forms are never its standard ones.
(1) Text holding every form of each value comes out with none of them, [SECRET:NAME] in each place, and everything else unchanged. Base64 at each alignment inside other bytes is masked too.
(2) The same text written into the pipe 7 bytes at a time gives the same output.
(3) The retired value is masked as [SECRET:BB_ONE].
(4) Mode 644, a bad line, a short value, or a file that names no value: exit 2, nothing of the input printed, and an error naming the file and the reason.
(5) The hook masks a Bash response that holds a value (the other fields kept), prints nothing for one that holds none, and withholds the response when the values file is at 644, and when its event is not JSON, is cut short inside a value, or cannot be read from stdin (printing nothing of its input). Each exits 0.
(6) No Claude Code settings file is left in the scratch HOME, and nothing printed holds a value in any form.
check-tests.sh and check-clippy.sh must pass.
